title: Divisorial fractional modules and their height-one lattices
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. Let $H(A)$ be the set of height-one primes of $A$, meaning nonzero prime ideals having no prime strictly between them and $(0)$. For $\mathfrak p\in H(A)$, the localization $A_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]; write $v_{\mathfrak p}:K^\times\to\mathbf Z$ for its normalized valuation. Let $(d_{\mathfrak p})_{\mathfrak p\in H(A)}$ be integers, zero except at finitely many primes, and write $D=\sum d_{\mathfrak p}[\mathfrak p]$. Define the concrete fractional submodule
$$I_A(D)=\{0\}\cup\{f\in K^\times: v_{\mathfrak p}(f)\ge d_{\mathfrak p}\text{ for all }\mathfrak p\in H(A)\}.$$
Then $I_A(D)$ is a nonzero finitely generated $A$-submodule of $K$, spans $K$ over $K$, and is reflexive: evaluation $I_A(D)\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(\operatorname{Hom}_A(I_A(D),A),A)$ is an isomorphism. For every $\mathfrak p\in H(A)$ and uniformizer $\pi_{\mathfrak p}$,
$$I_A(D)_{\mathfrak p}=\pi_{\mathfrak p}^{d_{\mathfrak p}}A_{\mathfrak p}\subset K.$$
For every multiplicative subset $S\subseteq A\setminus\{0\}$, localization satisfies $S^{-1}I_A(D)=I_{S^{-1}A}(D|_{S^{-1}A})$, where the restricted divisor retains exactly the height-one primes disjoint from $S$, with their coefficients. The associated sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}A$, defined on each basic open $D(s)$ by $I_A(D)_s$, is coherent [pqf-def-coherent] and of finite presentation, meaning locally the cokernel of a map between finite free module sheaves. Every nonzero finite reflexive submodule $L\subset K$ satisfies
$$L=\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\in H(A)}L_{\mathfrak p}\quad\text{inside }K.$$
In particular $A=\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\in H(A)}A_{\mathfrak p}$. If all $d_{\mathfrak p}\ge0$, then $I_A(D)$ is an ideal of $A$ and $\sqrt{I_A(D)}=\bigcap_{d_{\mathfrak p}>0}\mathfrak p$, with an empty intersection equal to $A$.

The localization, sign convention O(-D), and effective-ideal radical are explicit consequences of these constructions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-reflexive-height-one-intersection-criterion] to the finite free rank-one module $A$: both duals identify with $A$ by evaluation at $1$, and its evaluation map becomes the identity. It follows that $A=\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\in H(A)}A_{\mathfrak p}$ inside $K$. By [lem-trf-normal-domain-principal-divisor-kernel], these local rings are DVRs, membership is the condition $v_{\mathfrak p}(f)\ge0$, their units have valuation zero, and every nonzero $f\in K$ has nonzero valuations at only finitely many height-one primes. We use only these assertions, not its divisor-class notation.

proof.text:
The valuation inequality $v(f+g)\ge\min(v(f),v(g))$ (when $f+g
e0$), together with $v(af)=v(a)+v(f)$ and $v_{\mathfrak p}(a)\ge0$ for $0
e a\in A$, shows that $I=I_A(D)$ is an $A$-submodule of $K$. For each prime with $d_{\mathfrak p}
e0$ choose $0
e c_{\mathfrak p}\in\mathfrak p$. Set $a=\prod_{d_{\mathfrak p}<0}c_{\mathfrak p}^{-d_{\mathfrak p}}$ and $b=\prod_{d_{\mathfrak p}>0}c_{\mathfrak p}^{d_{\mathfrak p}}$. Both are nonzero, with empty products equal to $1$. Since $c_{\mathfrak p}/1$ lies in the maximal ideal of its DVR, its valuation there is at least $1$; at every other prime its valuation is nonnegative. Hence $v_{\mathfrak p}(a)+d_{\mathfrak p}\ge0$ and $v_{\mathfrak p}(b)\ge d_{\mathfrak p}$ for all $\mathfrak p$. Step 1 gives $aI\subseteq A$ and $bA\subseteq I$.

proof.text: Multiplication by $a$ is an $A$-linear isomorphism $I\cong aI$, and $aI\subseteq A$. Apply [lem-trf-noetherian-submodule-finitely-presented] with the finite module $F=A$ and submodule $aI$. Thus $I$ is finitely generated and finitely presented. The nonzero element $b\in I$ proves nonzeroness and spanning of $K$: every $x\in K$ is $(x/b)b$. In particular the map $K\otimes_A I\to K$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $x\mapsto(x/b)\otimes b$; the fraction relations show that this inverse is independent of the chosen element of $I$ used to represent a tensor.

Fix $\mathfrak p\in H(A)$. Fractions $h/u$ with $h\in I$ and $u\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ have $v_{\mathfrak p}(h/u)\ge d_{\mathfrak p}$ because $v_{\mathfrak p}(u)=0$. Conversely, take $0\ne f\in K$ satisfying that inequality. The bad set $B=\{\mathfrak q:v_{\mathfrak q}(f)<d_{\mathfrak q}\}$ is finite, by finite support of both $D$ and the valuations of $f$, and does not contain $\mathfrak p$. Distinct height-one primes are incomparable, so for each $\mathfrak q\in B$ choose $t_{\mathfrak q}\in\mathfrak q\setminus\mathfrak p$. Put $t=\prod_{\mathfrak q\in B}t_{\mathfrak q}^{d_{\mathfrak q}-v_{\mathfrak q}(f)}$. Then $t\notin\mathfrak p$, and at a bad prime the corresponding factor adds at least the required deficit. At every other prime all added valuations are nonnegative. Thus $tf\in I$ and $f=(tf)/t\in I_{\mathfrak p}$. Including zero proves $I_{\mathfrak p}=\{0\}\cup\{f:v_{\mathfrak p}(f)\ge d_{\mathfrak p}\}=\pi_{\mathfrak p}^{d_{\mathfrak p}}A_{\mathfrak p}$, the last equality following by applying the membership test to $f/\pi_{\mathfrak p}^{d_{\mathfrak p}}$.

source.place: Tag 0AVB, more-algebra-lemma-reflexive-over-normal, finite-support localization argument; explicit rank-one denominator correction

proof.text: The definition of $I$ and Step 4 give $I=\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\in H(A)}I_{\mathfrak p}$ in $K$. It is torsion free as a submodule of a field, and finite by Step 3. Therefore [lem-per-reflexive-height-one-intersection-criterion] proves reflexivity, for the actual evaluation map in the statement. If $L\subset K$ is any nonzero finite reflexive module, the same criterion gives $L=\bigcap L_{\mathfrak p}$: any $0\ne l\in L$ identifies $K\otimes_A L$ with $K$ by the multiplication map, whose inverse is $x\mapsto(x/l)\otimes l$. Thus these are the specified embedded intersections, not just abstract isomorphisms.

Put $A^{\prime}=S^{-1}A$. It is Noetherian and normal with fraction field $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian, lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], primes of $A^{\prime}$ correspond to primes of $A$ disjoint from $S$, and $(A^{\prime})_{S^{-1}\mathfrak p}=A_{\mathfrak p}$ inside $K$. Extension and contraction preserve inclusion (check generators of extended ideals), and every prime below one disjoint from $S$ is also disjoint from $S$. Thus height-one primes correspond exactly and their normalized valuations agree. Fractions $h/s$ with $h\in I$ satisfy every surviving inequality since $v_{\mathfrak p}(s)=0$ at primes disjoint from $S$. Conversely, let $0\ne f\in K$ satisfy those inequalities. Its finite bad set $B=\{\mathfrak q:v_{\mathfrak q}(f)<d_{\mathfrak q}\}$ consists entirely of primes meeting $S$. Choose $s_{\mathfrak q}\in S\cap\mathfrak q$ for each, and set $s=\prod_{\mathfrak q\in B}s_{\mathfrak q}^{d_{\mathfrak q}-v_{\mathfrak q}(f)}\in S$. Exactly as in Step 4, $sf\in I$, so $f=(sf)/s\in S^{-1}I$. Zero belongs to both sides. This proves the claimed equality for arbitrary $S$, including localization to a field.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] to $I$: it gives the quasi-coherent sheaf whose sections on $D(s)$ are $I_s$, with the stated localization restrictions. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], its finite and finitely presented global-section module $I$ (Step 3) makes this sheaf of finite type and of finite presentation, with the latter having precisely the local finite-free cokernel meaning in the item. Since $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] then proves coherence.

proof.text: If every $d_{\mathfrak p}\ge0$, Step 1 gives $I\subseteq A$, so the submodule is an ideal. For $x\in A\setminus\{0\}$ and $d_{\mathfrak p}>0$, membership $x\in\mathfrak p$ is equivalent to $v_{\mathfrak p}(x)\ge1$: localization contracts the maximal ideal back to $\mathfrak p$, and positive valuation means membership in that maximal ideal. If $x^N\in I$ for some $N\ge1$, then $Nv_{\mathfrak p}(x)\ge d_{\mathfrak p}>0$, so $x$ belongs to every such prime. Conversely, if $x$ belongs to all those primes, choose $N\ge1$ at least all the finitely many positive $d_{\mathfrak p}$. Then $Nv_{\mathfrak p}(x)\ge d_{\mathfrak p}$ at the positive coefficients; at all other primes $v_{\mathfrak p}(x)\ge0$. Hence $x^N\in I$. Zero satisfies both sides. With no positive coefficients $D=0$ and $I=A$, proving the empty-intersection convention too.
